annotations.text:
SIGNUP — two directions, pick one.

This is the weakest page on the live site: a 460px form on a wide empty field, for a product that is three apps.

A (left) keeps the single form and puts the three things people stall on beside it — which app do I get, is my health data safe, what does it cost.

B (right) asks who you are first, so the form is shorter and the next step is unambiguous. Costs an extra decision before anything is typed. The role cards are clickable — try them.

HOME — a gap, not a redesign.

The site describes each app well but never lets anyone compare them, so a visitor who is both a coach and a member has no way to work out what to install.

The dash is doing real work here: it means 'not this app's job', not 'feature missing' — same rule the product follows. Footnote says so.

SUPPORT — same words, better order.

No copy invented: every answer is lifted from the live page. What changed is that someone stuck can act in one glance — the email is a button at the top, response times are stated, and the questions are grouped and scannable rather than a single column of prose.

App reviewers land here too.
